messages.author: 94c2ffcec4dc149d
messages.subject: Compiler error on MacOS
parts:
I am trying to set up Nimble on MacOS 11.1, which has Apple clang version 12.0.0 (clang-1200.0.32.29).  As a starting point, I am trying to compile the dyes example.  However, I am getting a compiler error as shown below when it tries to link:

clang++ -std=gnu++11 -I"path/to/lib/R/include" -DNDEBUG -DR_NO_REMAP   -DEIGEN_MPL2_ONLY=1 -I"path/to/lib/R/library/nimble/include" -Wno-misleading-indentation -Wno-ignored-attributes -Wno-deprecated-declarations  -Ipath/to/include -Ipath/to/include/glib-2.0 -Ipath/to/include/gio-unix-2.0 -Ipath/to/lib/glib-2.0/include -D_REENTRANT -Ipath/to/include/freetype2 -Ipath/to/include/harfbuzz -Ipath/to/include/ncurses   -fPIC  -O2 -march=native -Ipath/to/include -Ipath/to/include/glib-2.0 -Ipath/to/include/gio-unix-2.0 -Ipath/to/lib/glib-2.0/include -D_REENTRANT -Ipath/to/include/freetype2 -Ipath/to/include/harfbuzz -Ipath/to/include/ncurses -march=native  -c dynamicRegistrations_01_26_15_58_22.cpp -o dynamicRegistrations_01_26_15_58_22.o

clang++ -std=gnu++11 -dynamiclib -Wl,-headerpad_max_install_names -undefined dynamic_lookup -single_module -multiply_defined suppress -Wl,-Rpath/to/lib/R/lib -Lpath/to/lib/R/lib -Lpath/to/lib -o dynamicRegistrations_01_26_15_58_22.so dynamicRegistrations_01_26_15_58_22.o -Lpath/to/lib/R/library/nimble/CppCode -lnimble -framework Accelerate -Wl,-Rpath/to/lib/R/lib -Lpath/to/lib/R/lib -lR -lintl -liconv -Wl,-framework -Wl,CoreFoundation

ld: unknown option: -Rpath/to/lib/R/lib

clang: error: linker command failed with exit code 1 (use -v to see invocation)

make[1]: *** [dynamicRegistrations_01_26_15_58_22.so] Error 1
Error: Failed to create the shared library.
Execution halted

On another MacOS machine with clang 10.0.1, there are no errors, but in that case -R is not part of the compiler command line used by Nimble; if it were, that linker would fail as well.

How do I figure out why Nimble is using -R when it should not be?  By the way, I compile all sorts of things on this machine, so I'm pretty certain the compiler itself is fine.

Thanks for your help.

Cheers,
Brook

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Compiler error on MacOS
parts:
hi Brook,

This is a bit puzzling as:
1) We don't have anything in how we configure compilation that would add the "-R" flag
2) Your output shows "path/to/lib", which seems like something inserted generically. I presume your machine does not actually have such a directory structure.

Do you have your own Makevars file (either in your home directory or in the directory used as the current working directory by R)? If so, values set in there might be affecting things. Or perhaps somehow values in a Makeconf file somewhere might be messing things up. We have a bit of info about this in Section 4.5.4 of the user manual. You might look in /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/etc. 

You might also check the nimble/CppCode/Makevars and nimble/make/Makevars files in your installed nimble directory to see if those might have been messed up somehow.

-chris
